observations: Photo shows a bare automotive engine assembly (block, head, intake manifold, injectors, alternator) sitting on a tarp on what appears to be an outdoor pavement/workshop floor.
Green paint marks are visible on multiple parts of the engine, a common grading/identification mark used on imported used engines.
No brand logo, engine code, or model sticker is legible anywhere in the frame.
A person's legs/feet are visible in the background, confirming an in-person outdoor setting, not a studio or dealer shot.
No accessories (ECU, wiring harness, turbo, etc.) or box/crate are shown alongside the engine.

claims.evidence: No markings, stickers, or paperwork in photo 0 indicate country of origin or import source; this is a sourcing claim that cannot be checked from a static image.

risks.risk: Whether the engine runs or has good compression
risks.proof: Video clip of the engine running/idling with audible sound, or a compression test reading

risks.risk: Which make, model, and displacement this engine fits
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code plate, casting number, or VIN sticker usually found on the block or head
risks.if_unproven: cannot be matched to any comparable price without this, since engine value varies enormously by vehicle fit

risks.risk: Mileage or usage history of the engine
risks.proof: Odometer photo from the donor vehicle or import paperwork

risks.risk: Completeness of the engine (missing sensors, turbo, ECU, wiring)
risks.proof: Additional photos from front, rear, and underside showing all connectors and accessories intact

risks.risk: Hidden damage such as cracks, oil leaks, or corrosion not visible under the green paint
risks.proof: Close-up photos of block seams, oil pan, and head gasket area in good light

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the engine code / casting number plate
Video of the engine running or at least turning over
Photos from additional angles (rear, underside, top) showing completeness
Any import or purchase documentation mentioning origin and mileage
response.reason: The engine's make, model, and displacement cannot be read from the single photo, and without that identification even a worst-case price is meaningless since engine values differ drastically by vehicle fit; a legible engine code or model photo is needed before pricing.
